exercises.label: Exercise C.R2 — Readiness: Build a weighted average
exercises.current_question: A quantity is $2$ in one quarter of cases and $6$ in the other three quarters. Find the average. Why is simply adding $2+6$ incorrect? Review if needed: sums and weights.

exercises.label: Exercise C.R3 — Readiness: Check an outer product
exercises.current_question: For column vector $v=(1,2)^\top$, compute $vv^\top$ and show that its quadratic form is nonnegative for every vector $w=(w_1,w_2)^\top$. Review if needed: outer products and PSD matrices.
exercises.current_worked_solution: The product is $vv^\top=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&4\end{bmatrix}$. For any $w$, its quadratic form is $(w_1+2w_2)^2\ge0$, so this matrix is positive semidefinite. exercises.label: Exercise C.S3 — Hard: A covariance calculation that detects dependence
exercises.current_question: Let $X$ be uniform on $\{-1,0,1\}$ and set $Y=X^2$. Compute the covariance matrix of $(X,Y)$. Are $X$ and $Y$ independent? Review if needed: this section and sets and events.

exercises.label: Exercise C.S15 — Hard: A bounded bias survives averaging
exercises.current_question: Let independent errors be uniform on $[0,2]$. A learner treats them as zero-mean noise and chooses $R=2$. Explain why the zero-mean sub-Gaussian condition fails. exercises.label: Exercise E.3 — When is it worth leaving home?
exercises.current_question: In the running example let the harvest reward be $h\gt0$ instead of $2$ (rest still pays $1$), with discount $\gamma\in(0,1)$. (a) Compute the value at home of the four deterministic stationary policies. (b) Show that leaving home is optimal if and only if $\gamma h\ge1$, and strictly better than staying if and only if $\gamma h\gt1$. (c) Interpret the condition. (d) With $h=2$ and the harvest cost $c=1$, for which $\gamma$ is "always harvest" both optimal and feasible for the budget $J_c\le4.5$?
exercises.current_worked_solution: (a) Write a policy as (action at home, action in the field). $(a,a)$ and $(a,b)$ rest forever: $V(1)=1/(1-\gamma)$. $(b,b)$ goes and harvests forever: $V(1)=\gamma h/(1-\gamma)$. $(b,a)$ shuttles back and forth with reward $0$: $V(1)=0$. (b) A finite discounted MDP has an optimal deterministic stationary policy (Section 3), so $V^\ast(1)=\max\{1/(1-\gamma),\,\gamma h/(1-\gamma),\,0\}$, and going is optimal exactly when $\gamma h/(1-\gamma)\ge1/(1-\gamma)$, i.e. $\gamma h\ge1$ (the shuttling policy, with value $0$, never wins). It is strictly better than resting exactly when $\gamma h\gt1$; at $\gamma h=1$ the two values coincide and both are optimal. (c) Leaving costs one step of reward $1$ now and delivers $h$ per step from the next step on; everything after that is the same stream shifted by one step. The trade is worth it when the one-step-delayed gain $\gamma h$ beats the immediate $1$. For $h=2$ the threshold is $\gamma=0.5$ (a tie): a more myopic agent (effective horizon below $2$ steps) strictly prefers to stay home. (d) $J_c=\sum_{t\ge1}\gamma^t=\gamma/(1-\gamma)\le4.5\iff\gamma\le4.5/5.5=9/11\approx0.818$. By (b) with $h=2$, harvesting is optimal for $\gamma\ge0.5$ (at $\gamma=0.5$ it ties with resting, and $J_c=1\le4.5$). So for $0.5\le\gamma\le9/11$ harvesting is optimal and feasible; for $\gamma\gt9/11$ the constrained optimum must mix, as in the occupancy example of Section 3 ($\gamma=0.9$, value $14$).

exercises.label: Exercise E.4 — The best baseline
exercises.current_question: One state, two actions, $\pi_\theta(1)=\sigma(\theta)=p$, reward $1$ for action $1$ and $0$ for action $0$. Consider $g_b=(r-b)\,\partial_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a)$ with $a\sim\pi_\theta$. (a) Show $\mathbb E\,g_b=p(1-p)$ for every $b$. (b) Find the $b$ that minimises $\mathrm{Var}\,g_b$ and the minimal variance. (c) Evaluate the variance at $p=0.8$ for $b=0$, $b=0.8$ and the optimal $b$. (d) Show that in general the variance-minimising constant baseline is $b^\ast=\mathbb E[r\,s^2]/\mathbb E[s^2]$ with $s$ the score.
exercises.current_worked_solution: (a) The scores are $s(1)=1-p$ and $s(0)=-p$, so $g_b=(1-b)(1-p)$ with probability $p$ and $g_b=bp$ with probability $1-p$. Then $\mathbb Eg_b=p(1-b)(1-p)+(1-p)bp=p(1-p)$: the $b$-terms cancel, as Step 5 of the walkthrough predicts. (b) Since $\mathbb Eg_b$ does not depend on $b$, minimise $\mathbb Eg_b^2=p(1-b)^2(1-p)^2+(1-p)b^2p^2$. Its derivative is $2p(1-p)\big[-(1-b)(1-p)+bp\big]=2p(1-p)\big[b-(1-p)\big]$, zero at $b^\ast=1-p$. Then $g_{b^\ast}=p(1-p)$ for both actions: variance $0$. (c) $p=0.8$: $b=0$ gives $g\in\{0.2,0\}$, variance $0.8\cdot0.04-0.16^2=0.0064$; $b=0.8$ gives $g\in\{0.04,0.64\}$, variance $0.8\cdot0.0016+0.2\cdot0.4096-0.0256=0.0576$; $b^\ast=0.2$ gives variance $0$. The average reward $0.8$ is nine times worse than no baseline. (d) $\mathrm{Var}\,g_b=\mathbb E[(r-b)^2s^2]-(\mathbb Eg_b)^2$ and the second term does not depend on $b$; the first is the quadratic $\mathbb E[r^2s^2]-2b\,\mathbb E[rs^2]+b^2\,\mathbb E[s^2]$, minimised at $b^\ast=\mathbb E[rs^2]/\mathbb E[s^2]$. Here $\mathbb E[rs^2]=p(1-p)^2$ and $\mathbb E[s^2]=p(1-p)^2+(1-p)p^2=p(1-p)$, so $b^\ast=1-p$. Rewards are weighted by squared score: the rarely chosen action, whose score is large, dominates the baseline.

reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-basics: Probability law normalized/nonnegative; stated expectations integrable and variances/covariances have finite second moments. Nondegenerate Gaussian support requires positive variance; zero variance is a point mass.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-conditioning: Positive-probability conditioning event for ratios; conditional expectations integrable, L2 for squared-error optimality. Policies randomize with normalized nonnegative weights.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-markov: Finite nonnegative row-stochastic transition matrix; stationary/ergodic and transient inverse conclusions use their stated class/transience assumptions. Independent centered AR innovations and finite moments where used.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-gaussian: Joint Gaussian law; covariance symmetric positive semidefinite; conditioning observation covariance invertible; observation noise independent with positive variance where precision inverses are used.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-inequalities: Positive tail thresholds; finite second moment for Chebyshev, centered finite MGF for sub-Gaussian bounds; independent samples/common mean/bounded intervals for Hoeffding. Degenerate interval/R=0 cases handled separately.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-high-probability: Failure budgets nonnegative; target confidence delta in (0,1); finite/countable unions do not require independence, product formulas do. Initial safety has probability one when horizons start at t=1.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-martingales: Adapted integrable process; predictable coefficients and conditional zero-mean increments; boundedness/uniform-integrability hypotheses for optional stopping as stated. Ville threshold positive; Donsker iid centered positive finite variance.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-information: Normalized distributions, absolute continuity/support for finite directional KL, positive-definite Gaussian covariance for entropy, finite first moments for Wasserstein; positive observation noise and attained maximum or supremum for information gain.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-quantiles-risk: Loss integrable; confidence alpha in (0,1); lower-quantile definition and fractional atom handling for CVaR. Coherence/optimization claims under their stated definitions.
reviewed_section_assumptions.pr-testing: IID Bernoulli episodes/fixed tested policy for binomial confidence; scenario regularity/convexity where used; exchangeable calibration/test scores and distinct-score qualifier; positive Beta shape parameters and rank range.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-state-space: ODE local existence/uniqueness from local Lipschitz regularity, maximal intervals; equilibrium and linearization conclusions distinguish continuous/discrete time and local nonlinear stability.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-linear: Finite-dimensional linear system; continuous Hurwitz vs discrete Schur distinctions; Jordan/transient amplification and exact sampling use matching time domain.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-lyapunov: Positive-definite certificate with appropriate strict decrease, differentiability and ODE existence; nonempty complete invariant domain for contraction. Rational rounded bounds must round outward.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-comparison: Locally Lipschitz comparison function/trajectory regularity; positive rates and properly signed barrier inequalities; feasible attained control supremum for feedback existence.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-feedback: Stabilizability/detectability and positive-definite input cost for LQR as stated; constrained actuator limits distinguished from unconstrained gains. Integral state may maintain nonzero input at zero error.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-frequency: Causal stable/zero-state response for induced gains; correct continuous/discrete convention; nonnegative storage and zero initial condition for energy bounds.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-absolute-stability: Feedback well-posed/causal under relevant theorem; sector slopes/nonlinearity equilibrium matched; strict small-gain condition is sufficient, and failed condition gives no instability conclusion.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-realization: Finite-dimensional state-space dimensions; controllability rank characterizes reachability with unrestricted controls; coordinate transform invertible; Gramian horizon positive.
reviewed_section_assumptions.sys-optimal-control: Admissible inputs/disturbances and state constraints explicitly modeled; local Lipschitz/tangent assumptions for viability; viscosity boundary/comparison conditions; MPC closed constraints, optimizer attainment, terminal feasibility and positive-definite decrease for convergence.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-bandits: Bounded reward/stationary arm assumptions for UCB1; positive pull counts; comparator static vs dynamic explicitly distinguished; GP confidence/acquisition does not by itself certify safety.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-mdp: Finite MDP with nonempty available action sets, normalized transitions/initial law, bounded rewards/costs and discount in [0,1). Expected discounted cost differs from almost-sure trajectory safety.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-bellman: Finite discounted MDP and fixed stationary policy where evaluated; normalized occupancy flow; positive discounted occupancy converse requires gamma>0, while gamma=0 tests only time zero.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-dp: Finite nonempty action set and stochastic transition rows; discount in [0,1) for contraction/unique fixed point; undiscounted transient examples handled separately.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-policy-gradient: Positive C1 policy near parameter; environment rewards/transitions/initial distribution independent of parameter; bounded discounted finite MDP; baseline action-independent; positive-definite Fisher/nonzero gradient/positive radius for inverse trust-region formula, with zero-gradient case separate.
reviewed_section_assumptions.rl-modern: Valid MDP samples and step sizes in (0,1], Robbins--Monro conditions/visitation for tabular convergence; entropy temperature positive and finite action set; offline/ensemble uncertainty is not an out-of-distribution certificate.
reviewed_section_assumptions.nn-basics: Layer dimensions consistent; activation derivatives only where differentiable; input vs parameter gradients distinguished; slope and norm inequalities in matching coordinates.
reviewed_section_assumptions.nn-architectures: Matching convolution/attention/residual dimensions; positive normalization standard deviation; global Lipschitz/contraction proof required for a global equilibrium guarantee.
reviewed_section_assumptions.nn-robustness: A proved global or local Lipschitz constant on the relevant set; L>0 for radius division, zero-L constant case separate; strict radius/sign margin and specified norm; finite attacks/ray searches are numerical evidence, not universal distance proofs.
